# THE World Reputation Rankings 2022 released

**Asia’s global recognition grows in the *Times Higher Education* World Reputation Rankings 2022**

- **Harvard University retains its top spot for the 12th consecutive- year**
- **It is the** **first time that there are two Asian universities in the top 10**, but not the first time that Tsinghua or Tokyo are in the top 10 - **Tsinghua University in China in 9th place and The University of Tokyo in Japan in 10th place**
- **China has nine universities in the top 100,** up from seven last year
- **Imperial College London joins the top 20 in 14th place,** up from 23rd
- **Technical University of Munich leaps forwards to lead Germany’s universities in 33rd place,** up from 45th

*Times Higher Education* (*THE*), the trusted global data partner for higher education, has today announced the results of its annual World Reputation Rankings 2022, listing the world’s top 200 most prestigious universities as judged by academics.

A record 29,606​ experienced, published academics around the world cast 420,204​ votes to inform the ranking, giving a clear picture of those universities across the globe that they believe have the best reputation for research and teaching. The Reputation Rankings is comprised of 211 universities from 32 countries. The Rankings includes 211 universities in a top 200 table because some of the institutions’ scores resulted in tied places within group bands.

**#THEReputation #THEUniRankings**

**Phil Baty, Chief Knowledge Officer, *Times Higher Education*, commented:**

*“In higher education, reputation really matters: it helps attract inward investment; it helps draw-in quality partners for strategic advancement; and**,* *perhaps above all else, it is key to attracting talent, among both academics and of course the many millions of prospective students who have more and more choice of where to study. It is subjective, and it is not always fair, but it has real currency with tangible effects.”*

**Please note: if you reproduce these rankings or any part, please attribute to “*Times Higher Education* World Reputation Rankings”, and link to the full list of the Rankings on our website:** <https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/2022/reputation-ranking>

***THE*** **World Reputation Rankings 2022 Top 10 table (scroll down for full** **r****anking of top 200 universities)**

| **Institution** | **Country/region** | **2022 Rank** | **2021 Rank** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Harvard University | United States | 1 | 1 |
| Massachusetts Institute of Technology | United States | 2 | 2 |
| Stanford University | United States | 3 | 4 |
| University of Oxford | United Kingdom | 4 | 3 |
| University of Cambridge | United Kingdom | 5 | 5 |
| University of California, Berkeley | United States | 6 | 6 |
| Princeton University | United States | 7 | 7 |
| Yale University | United States | 8 | 8 |
| Tsinghua University | China | 9 | 10 |
| The University of Tokyo | Japan | 10 | 13 |

At the top of the table, Harvard University and Massachusetts Institute of Technology retain their respective number one and number two spots, while Stanford University pushes University of Oxford into 4th place to take 3rd position.

China continues its impressive climb up the Reputation Rankings with nine universities in the top 100, up from seven last year. Tsinghua University leads the way, rising to 9th position from 10th last year, and Peking University moves up to 13th place from 15th. In the top 50, Shanghai Jiao Tong University leaps forward to 28th position up from joint 50th, and Fudan University rises to 39th place up from group band 51-60. China’s steady progress in global recognition mirrors its impressive rise in the *Times Higher Education* World University Rankings.

Elsewhere in Asia, The University of Tokyo rejoins the top 10 in 10th place, after it dropped to 13th position last year, and National University of Singapore enters the top 20 in 19th place, up from 24th.

The United States has one less university in the top 10 this year, but continues to dominate the top of the table with six universities represented in the top 10; and Harvard University leads the Rankings for the 12th consecutive year. The US experiences a few rises and falls within the table, but overall proves its top universities remain prestigious in the eyes of scholars across the globe.

In the United Kingdom, Imperial College London joins the top 20 in 14th place, up from 23rd, and University of Bristol enters the top 100 in group band 81-90, up from 101-125. However, the UK has also experienced some drops at the top of the table with UCL falling out of the top 20 into 25th place, down from 17th, and London School of Economics and Political Science slipping to 37th place, down from 26th.

In mainland Europe, Technical University of Munich has leapt forward to 33rd place to lead Germany’s representation in the Rankings, up from 45th place. Sorbonne University in France rejoins the top 50 in joint 50th position, up from group band 51-60, and Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands continues to climb the top of the table, rising to 43rd place up from joint 50th. Meanwhile, in Switzerland, ETH Zurich creeps ever closer to the top 10, ranking 12th up from 18th.

**Mark Sudbury, Head of the World 100 Reputation Network, a group of communications chiefs at leading universities around the world, commented:**

*“With more than 420,204 votes cast in total, the rankings represent just the tip of a mountain of data that illuminates the way in which the academic community judges the reputation of global universities.*

*“Institutions are increasingly interested in understanding their strength in key subject areas and regions to support their strategic development. **About the *Times Higher Education* World Reputation Rankings**

The *Times Higher Education* World Reputation Rankings are created using the world’s largest invitation-only academic opinion survey. The Academic Reputation Survey, available in 12 languages, uses United Nations data as a guide to ensure that the response coverage is as representative of world scholarship as possible. It is also evenly spread across academic disciplines. It is by far the most comprehensive academic survey underpinning university rankings across the world, with over 29,000 respondents in 2022.

The questionnaire targets only experienced, published scholars, who offer their views on excellence in research and teaching within their disciplines and at institutions with which they are familiar. The resulting data combined with our methodology allows *THE* to create a ranking of the world’s strongest academic brands, as viewed by those who work in the field. <https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/world-reputation-rankings-2022-methodology> 

The Academic Reputation Survey is one of the metrics taken into account in compiling our flagship rankings, the *Times Higher Education* World University Rankings.
